questions.text: In residual vector quantization, what does each codebook after the first quantize?

options.A: The original waveform independently of the earlier codebooks.
options.B: The remaining error after the earlier quantized approximations.
options.C: The text transcript corresponding to the audio frame.
options.D: The decoder’s final waveform after resampling.

questions.explanation: Each successive codebook approximates the residual left by earlier stages; the selected code vectors are summed to reconstruct the encoder representation.

questions.text: Two codecs reconstruct held-out audio equally well, but you need tokens for text-conditioned speech generation. Which additional property should you evaluate?

options.A: Whether the codec output filenames contain the transcript.
options.B: Whether its decoder can run without any input tokens.
options.C: Whether all codebooks have identical token sequences.
options.D: Whether the tokens expose content structure that a language model can learn.

questions.explanation: Reconstruction fidelity alone does not establish suitability for generation. Useful linguistic structure, including semantic-acoustic organization, can help the language model predict speech.

questions.text: Given codes.shape == (1, 8, 125), the code sets semantic = codes[:, 0] and acoustic = codes[:, 1:]. What are their shapes?
questions.explanation: Integer indexing selects and removes the codebook axis for semantic; slicing retains that axis with the remaining seven codebooks for acoustic.
